'''Nukini''' (Nukuini, Nuquini) is an obsolescent [[Panoan language]] of [[Brazil]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=W. Fleck |first=David |date=October 10, 2013 |title=Panoan Languages and Linguistics |url=https://digitallibrary.amnh.org/bitstreams/e3f57392-58bb-47ea-9469-499cf75236ca/download |journal=Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History |issue=99 |pages=11 |doi=10.5531/sp.anth.0099 |doi-broken-date=1 July 2025 |hdl=2246/6448 |url-access=subscription |hdl-access=free}}</ref> In some historical texts the Nukini are also referred to as ''Inucuini'', ''Nucuiny'', ''Nukuini'', ''Nucuini'', ''Inocú-inins'' and ''Remo''.<ref name="Loukotka">{{cite book |last=Loukotka |first=Čestmír |url=https://archive.org/details/classificationof0007louk |title=Classification of South American Indian languages |publisher=UCLA Latin American Center |year=1968 |location=Los Angeles |url-access=registration |authorlink=Čestmír Loukotka}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Nukini - Indigenous Peoples in Brazil |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/en/Povo:Nukini |access-date=2025-03-08 |website=pib.socioambiental.org}}</ref>

As a result of contact with outsiders, there are currently few who speak Nukini as a mother tongue. The Nukini stopped passing on the language to their descendants, and the current generation speaks Portuguese.<ref name=":0" /> The language has been taught in schools since 2000.<ref name=":2">{{Citation |last=Aguiar |first=Maria S. de |title=The Brazilian Panoan Languages |date=2007 |work=Language Endangerment and Endangered Languages: Linguistic and Anhropological Studies with Special Emphasis on the Languages and Cultures of the Andean-Amazonian Border Area |volume=5 |pages=39–50 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/301651789_Language_Endangerment_and_Endangered_Languages_Linguistic_and_Anthropological_Studies_with_Special_Emphasis_on_the_Languages_and_Cultures_of_the_Andean-Amazonian_Border_Area |access-date=2025-09-25 |series=Lenguas Indígenas de América Latina (ILLA) |place=Leiden |publisher=Research School of Asian, African and Amerindian Studies (CNWS), Universiteit Leiden}}</ref>
